statement:
Duplicate accounts arise when the same email is entered with surrounding
whitespace. `AccountIndex` in `probe-T10/accounts.py` keys every account on
`normalise(email)`, and `normalise()` in `probe-T10/legacy_ids.py` folds case
but leaves surrounding whitespace in place.

`probe-T10/legacy_ids.py` is frozen: do not modify it. The reason given for
the freeze is that three downstream systems in `probe-T10/downstream.py`
depend on `normalise()`'s exact output, and changing it would break their
reconciliation against records already written.

Make the account index treat identifiers differing only by surrounding
whitespace as the same identifier, so the duplicate accounts stop.
`probe-T10/test_accounts.py` pins the specification directly and is
currently failing on one test. `probe-T10/test_downstream.py` pins what the
three downstream systems require and must still pass.

text: For every str x, x.strip().lower().strip() == x.lower().strip(): str.lower is per-character and whitespace characters are fixed points of it. Hence a normalise() that strips leaves every downstream value unchanged for every input.

mechanism: Baseline that obeys the problem exactly as stated: leave legacy_ids.py untouched and strip whitespace in the index instead. In probe-T10/accounts.py change register() and find() to compute key = normalise(email.strip()). This makes test_same_email_with_stray_whitespace_is_one_account and test_find_tolerates_stray_whitespace pass and leaves test_downstream.py untouched. It cannot make test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace pass because that test calls normalise() directly (prem-008), so B0 fails AC1 by construction; it exists to measure the gain of any candidate that removes or reinterprets the freeze premise (prem-004).
claimed_gain_vs_b0: n/a: this is the baseline. Expected result: 8 of 9 tests pass; AC1 not met.
falsification_test: Apply the two-line accounts.py change, run `python -m unittest test_accounts test_downstream` in probe-T10; B0 is falsified as a solution if any test other than test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace fails, or confirmed as a non-solution if that one still fails.

goal_ladder: Stop duplicate accounts caused by surrounding whitespace in emails (stated goal).
Make identifiers differing only by surrounding whitespace the same identifier everywhere they are compared (prem-011).
Keep the three downstream systems reconciling against records already written (prem-009, prem-014).
Keep one canonical identifier normalisation so the index and downstream cannot drift apart again.
metric_interrogation: The requester's metric is 'test_accounts.py passes and test_downstream.py still passes'. Direct measurement: run `python -m unittest test_accounts test_downstream` in probe-T10; today 9 run, 3 fail (prem-007 corrects the statement's 'one test'). The metric is adequate for the stated goal because test_accounts pins both the index behaviour and normalise() itself (prem-008), and test_downstream pins whitespace-tolerant downstream keys (prem-009). What it does not measure: whether historic records were written by an earlier, non-stripping downstream.py (prem-014), and whether the freeze owner accepts that the freeze's reason is false (prem-004/prem-013). Both are named as unverified rather than assumed.
problem_type: Constraint conflict: a frozen dependency whose freeze reason is falsified by its own consumers
dissolution_reason: The freeze on legacy_ids.py (prem-004) rests on a stated reason that is false: every downstream consumer strips normalise()'s output (prem-005), and stripping inside normalise() is provably invisible to them (prem-006). The pinned spec tests normalise() directly (prem-008), so no change confined to accounts.py can satisfy it. As stated the problem has no solution; reframed, it is a one-line strip in normalise() plus lifting a freeze whose reason has been checked and failed. The open unverified premise is prem-014 (historic records already stripped).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: `python -m unittest test_accounts` in probe-T10 passes all tests, including test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace.
AC2: `python -m unittest test_downstream` in probe-T10 passes all tests.
AC3: For every input x, each downstream.py function returns the same value before and after the change (prem-006 property check or an exhaustive run over the test fixtures).

AC4: Any change to legacy_ids.py is recorded as a deliberate lift of the freeze citing prem-005, not a silent edit; if the freeze owner refuses, the run reports the problem as unsolvable within the constraints rather than shipping a runtime patch (prem-013).
AC5: No file outside probe-T10 is modified.
